subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & close timeline — MIG vs full GPU scaling
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Hayes <taylor.hayes@acmedyn.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & close timeline — MIG vs full GPU scaling

Hi Taylor —

Thanks for taking the meeting last week. Per our discussion, attached is a focused MAP that ties the performance benchmark plan to the close timeline and procurement milestones. Key ask: we want to validate 99th-pct TTFT and steady-state throughput at your target concurrency (200–500 concurrent inference sessions) before finalizing Dedicated capacity sizing.

What we included in the MAP (attachments):
- Evaluation plan (sprint schedule + measurement specs) — latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT (time-to-first-token), tokens/sec throughput, and memory/KV cache behaviour.
- Hardware matrix: A100 (40GB), H100 (80GB), L40S (48GB) and MIG partitions (1g/2g/7g profiles) vs full-GPU runs.
- Test harness config: model checkpoints to use, sequence length envelope (avg 128, 95th 512), batching strategy, and warm-up policies.
- Success criteria to unblock procurement: p99 TTFT <= 600ms for 95% of requests and sustained tokens/sec that supports 500 concurrent sessions with <= 150ms variance across runs.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (Jun 21–27): lab setup, access to sample dataset, baseline runs on A100 and H100 (full GPU).
- Week 2 (Jun 28–Jul 4): MIG partitioning tests, L40S runs, and mixed-fleet stress tests at target concurrency.
- Week 3 (Jul 5–11): stability + regression runs, finalize results, and handoff to procurement for Dedicated sizing.

Can you confirm the following so we lock the MAP?
1) Who from Acme will be the point of contact for dataset access and procurement timelines?
2) Are there any regulatory constraints that will require on-prem validation instead of cloud-hosted runs?
3) Preferred time window for the system load tests (we recommend a 4hr continuous run during off-peak).

I'll schedule the first lab session once I hear back.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0137

Attachments: map-performance-plan.xlsx (workbook), h100-a100-l40s-benchmark-results.csv (initial), proposal-acme-v2.pdf (proposal draft)

From: Taylor Hayes <taylor.hayes@acmedyn.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Chopra <samir@acmedyn.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:42 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation & close timeline — MIG vs full GPU scaling

Rishi —

Thanks, this looks great and very practical. Quick answers:
- Samir will be the technical POC for datasets and will handle credentials (cc'd).
- No regulatory hold; cloud-hosted runs are OK for the benchmark phase.
- We can do the continuous 4hr load window any night 22–24 Jun (we prefer 2300–0300 PT).

Two clarifying items from our infra team:
1) We want to understand the trade-offs between MIG partitions vs full-GPU for tail latency at 200–500 concurrency. Our expectation is MIG improves utilization but risks higher p99 — we want the empirical numbers.
2) For L40S: we run some inference workloads with 8-bit quantized weights; confirm whether your runtime will auto-select optimized kernels and whether the tests will include quantized model variants.

If you can add short acceptance criteria for MIG (e.g., allowable p99 degradation vs full-GPU), we can sign off on the MAP and lock the procurement timeline.

Best,
Taylor
Taylor Hayes | Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Dynamics
Taylor.Hayes@acmedyn.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MAP: Performance evaluation & close timeline — MIG vs full GPU scaling

Laura / Marissa —

Forwarding Acme's confirmation and the two technical asks. Please see inline notes: 

> Two clarifying items from our infra team:
> 1) We want to understand the trade-offs between MIG partitions vs full-GPU for tail latency at 200–500 concurrency.
> 2) For L40S: confirm whether your runtime will auto-select optimized kernels and whether the tests will include quantized model variants.

My notes:
- Plan to run a side-by-side p99-focused experiment: identical workload, identical batching policy, compare full GPU (A100/H100/L40S) vs MIG with 1g/2g/7g partitions. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, TTFT, tokens/sec, and memory fragmentation metrics.
- Runtime does auto-kernel selection and we will run quantized variants (int8/4-bit where supported) and include those runs in the acceptance matrix.

Request: can you provision the following in the lab for Week 1/2?
- 2x H100 (full), 2x A100 (full), 3x L40S (full) with ability to create 1g/2g/7g MIG slices on the H100/A100 nodes.
- Access to a steady synthetic load generator configured for variable seq lengths (avg 128, outliers 512).

I'll update the MAP with explicit acceptance thresholds for MIG (see draft below) and share with Acme this afternoon.

– R

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 14:06:28 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP: Performance evaluation & close timeline — MIG vs full GPU scaling

Rishi —

We can support the lab requests; I reserved nodes and will coordinate with infra to enable MIG profiles. Notes on instrumentation:
- We'll enable token-level tracing for a subset of runs (10% sampling) to capture TTFT components (queue/warmup/first-token issuance).
- I'll add a post-run sanity check that computes variance across runs and flags noise > 10% for re-run.

Proposed MIG acceptance (draft):
- p99_latency_mig <= p99_latency_full + 20% (absolute bound: p99 <= 900ms) for the same concurrency and batching policy. If the p99 delta > 20% we consider MIG unsuitable for primary fleet but it can be used for background workloads.
- TTFT: MIG TTFT <= 1.25x TTFT_full for 95% of warm requests.

I'll push the lab reservation details and a short runbook into the MAP spreadsheet.

Laura
VP, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Hayes <taylor.hayes@acmedyn.com>, Samir Chopra <samir@acmedyn.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 17:03:12 -0700
Subject: Results: MAP benchmark summary & recommendation (A100 / H100 / L40S, MIG vs full)

Taylor / Samir —

We completed the MAP runs and here's the concise summary aligned to the acceptance criteria. Full CSV attached (h100-a100-l40s-benchmark-results.csv) and the MAP workbook has the runbook + charts.

Executive summary (short):
- Best tail latency: H100 (full) — p99: 410ms, TTFT median: 160ms, tokens/sec @500 concurrent: 62k
- A100 (full): p99: 520ms, TTFT median: 210ms, tokens/sec @500 concurrent: 54k
- L40S (full, quantized int8): p99: 610ms, TTFT median: 240ms, tokens/sec @500 concurrent: 58k (good throughput, slightly higher p99)
- MIG (H100 partitioned 1g/2g/7g, balanced allocation): p99 range: 520–760ms (varies by slice size), TTFT median: 210–290ms, tokens/sec aggregate @500 concurrent: 49k (higher utilization but lower absolute throughput)

Acceptance check vs proposed thresholds:
- MIG p99 delta vs H100 full: worst-case delta = 760 - 410 = +85% (exceeds 20% threshold) for worst-case 1g slices under high seq-length variance; for 7g slices delta is +27% (marginally above 20%).
- TTFT: MIG median up to 1.4x of H100_full in smallest slices (exceeds 1.25x limit); larger slices (7g) remain within 1.15x.

Operational notes:
- Quantized L40S delivered solid tokens/sec with lower GPU cost per token; however p99 is higher than H100 by ~50–100ms which may matter for interactive use cases.
- MIG is attractive for utilization (cost) but small slices (1g/2g) show significant tail risk at your worst-case sequence distribution. We recommend a hybrid fleet: majority full H100 for interactive low-latency paths, supplemented by L40S quantized instances for background or cost-sensitive batch workloads; use 7g MIG slices only for mid-priority traffic.

Recommended next steps to close (timeline):
1) Lock Dedicated order: 6x H100 full nodes + 8x L40S quantized nodes (proposal attached) — Rishi to follow up with procurement paperwork this week.
2) Run one production-like 8hr soak on the proposed fleet mix (tentative Jul 7) to validate stability at scale.
3) Add a small canary routing policy (10% traffic) to L40S for 2 weeks post-provisioning and monitor p99 TTFT and errors.

Please reply with sign-off or tweaks and we'll initiate DocuSign for the Dedicated order.

Thanks for the collaboration — great work getting this scoped and run quickly.

– Rishi

Attachments: h100-a100-l40s-benchmark-results.csv, proposal-acme-v2.pdf
